extName.message: Enhancer for Plane — Quick Open & Issue Templates
extName.description: Extension name shown in the Chrome Web Store and browser.

extShort.description: The brand on its own — the name you can say out loud. Used where a name has to be short: the popup and settings headers, and the toolbar tooltip. extName adds the searchable half after it.

extDesc.message: Issue templates, quick open by key, copy reference, and a focus mode that hides the side panels — inside the Plane UI.
extDesc.description: Short description shown in the Chrome Web Store, and the extension's own description in chrome://extensions. Features and where they appear, nothing else: an extension not touching the server is not news, "the open-source Jira alternative" only spent characters on a reader already looking at a Plane extension, and the searchable spellings (makeplane, plane.so) sit at the foot of the store description.

cmdToggleFocus.message: Focus mode: hide or show the side panels
cmdToggleFocus.description: Shown in chrome://extensions/shortcuts, where the user can rebind the key. It has to say what the shortcut does with no surrounding UI to lean on.

optTagline.message:
Quick open, issue templates, copy reference, focus mode, style rules.
Quick open works on Jira and Linear too.
optTagline.description: Sub-line under the settings header: the feature list, then the one thing about it that surprises people. No lead clause — the product name is directly above it, and "fills the gaps in Plane" was doing its work in the store listing anyway. Order matches extName: quick open first. Two lines is the budget, one sentence each, and the harness measures it in both locales.

optFeedback.description: Header link to the GitHub issue tracker. Deliberately an invitation, not "Report an issue" — most of what arrives is an idea or a question, and the narrower wording turned the tracker into a place you only visit when something is broken.

optChangelog.description: Tooltip on the version number in the Settings header, which links to CHANGELOG.md. The number itself is the link because "what is in this version" is the question a version number raises, and a fourth named link in that row would cost the row a line.

optDomainsDesc.message: The extension runs only on these domains, one per line. *.example.com covers every subdomain, and a pasted address is cut down to its hostname. Saving asks Chrome for access to each new one.

optDomainsAll.message: Run on all sites (ignore the list below)

optDomainsTip.message: Tip: to enable the current tab's Plane instance, open the toolbar popup and click “Enable on this site.”

optFocusDesc.message: Hides what you do not need while you read or write a work item. Turn it on with Alt+Shift+F (macOS ⌥+⇧+F), the toggle beside the item's key, or the popup switch. It switches on the rules below marked “Only while focus mode is on”.

optRulesTitle.description: Was "Style rules (width / length)" while every shipped rule set a width. Focus mode's presets set display and padding in the same list, so the parenthetical had become a promise the card no longer keeps; the description under it says what a rule is instead.

optRulesDesc.message: Changes how a page looks: a CSS selector, a property and a value, applied with !important. Type the value with its unit, such as 320px. If Plane renames a class, edit the selector.

optRulesEmpty.message: No rules yet. Click “Add rule” to start.

optPresetDescFull.message: Work item description: show all of it
optPresetDescFull.description: Plane clips a long description behind a Show all toggle; this preset undoes the clipping.

optPresetDescToggle.message: Work item description: hide the fade and Show all
optPresetDescToggle.description: Show all is Plane's own label for that toggle (모두 보기 in Plane's Korean UI).

optPresetFocusProps.message: Focus: hide the work item properties panel

optPresetFocusWidth.message: Focus: centre the body at a reading width
optPresetFocusWidth.description: Ships switched off — capping the line length is a preference, unlike hiding a panel the user just asked to hide.

optRuleFocusOnly.message: Only while focus mode is on

optRuleHealthOk.description: Beside a rule that is working. An absolute time, like the sync status uses — a redesign shows up as one stale date beside rules that all read today.

optRuleHealthCold.description: Beside a rule whose selector has been checked several times without ever finding an element.

optRuleHealthWarn.message: Never matched anything yet: $COUNT$ of these rules. Plane's markup may have changed — edit the selector, or pick the element again.
optRuleHealthWarn.description: Above the rule list. Phrased so it reads correctly for a count of one. One line, no break: a script reads it, and a status line is not a pre-line sink.

optTplAnchorOk.description: In the templates card, when the button has found a description toolbar to sit on. Same shape as optRuleHealthOk.

optTplAnchorCold.message: The Template button has not found a toolbar to sit on yet, on $COUNT$ work item pages. Plane's layout may have changed.
optTplAnchorCold.description: In the templates card, once enough work item pages (by address, with an editable description) have gone by without the button being placed. One line, no break: a status line is not a pre-line sink.

optTplAnchorLost.message: The Template button was last placed $TIME$, and has not been on the last $COUNT$ work item pages. Plane's layout may have changed.
optTplAnchorLost.description: In the templates card: the button worked before, and a run of work item pages since has gone by without it. One line, no break.

optCopyAnchorOk.description: In the copy reference card, when the button has found a work item header to sit beside.

optCopyAnchorCold.message: The copy button has not found a work item header yet, on $COUNT$ work item pages. Plane's layout may have changed.
optCopyAnchorCold.description: In the copy reference card, once enough work item pages (by address) have gone by without the button being placed. One line, no break.

optCopyAnchorLost.message: The copy button was last placed $TIME$, and has not been on the last $COUNT$ work item pages. Plane's layout may have changed.
optCopyAnchorLost.description: In the copy reference card: the button worked before, and a run of work item pages since has gone by without it. One line, no break.

optTplDesc1.message: Fills a work item's title and description in one go, from the “Template” button beside “Attach” in the description toolbar, or Alt/⌥+T while you type.

optTplEmpty.message: No templates yet. Click “Add template” to start.

optTplTitlePh.message: Title (e.g. [Bug] — leave empty to skip the title)

optVarsDesc.message: Your own values for {{var.name}}, in your templates and synced ones alike. A synced template that says {{var.team}} fills in each person's own value.

optVarsEmpty.message: No variables yet. Click “Add variable” to start.

msgVarBadName.message: Use letters, numbers, hyphen or underscore only.

msgVarDupe.message: Another variable already uses this name.

msgVarLimit.message: Up to $MAX$ variables. Remove one to add another.

msgSrcLimit.message: Up to $MAX$ sync sources. Remove one to add another.

optSyncDesc.message:
Pulls shared templates from a URL and keeps them up to date.
They are read-only here.
Edit them at the source.

optSyncFormatDesc.message: Checked when the browser starts, on each source's schedule, and when this page opens. A file on the same domain as Plane needs no separate access prompt. The file is a flat list of templates, each with its own group. The top-level name is used when a source's name is left blank.

optSrcUrlPh.description: Placeholder text: an example URL. Nothing here is prose.

optBackupDesc1.message: Export every setting to a JSON file, or import one. An import fills the form, and applies when you Save.

optBackupDesc2.message:
The file holds your domains, source addresses and variable values in plain text, so if any of them is private, keep the file internal.
Synced templates are not in it: they download again from their source after you Save.

optStorageNote.message:
Settings sync across your devices via Chrome, which allows ~100 KB in total.
Templates are stored in blocks of ~8 KB, so any one template has to fit a single block.

msgInvalidSrcUrl.message: A source URL must start with http:// or https://

msgSrcEnterUrl.message: Enter a URL, then Save to sync.

msgSrcNotSynced.message: Not synced yet — Save, then “Sync now”.

msgSrcSkipped.description: Appended to msgSrcSynced, so the leading space is deliberate — without it the two run together as "12 templates(3 skipped".

msgSrcLastGood.description: Appended to msgSrcFailed. Leading space deliberate, as with msgSrcSkipped.

msgSrcHidden.description: Appended to a source's summary line. Leading space deliberate.

msgChangedElsewhere.message: Settings changed elsewhere (e.g. the picker). Reload this page to apply them — unsaved edits will be lost.

msgLoadedPicked.message: Loaded the rule added by the picker.

msgFeedNamePrompt.message: Name this set of templates. A teammate sees it as the source's name unless they rename it. Leave empty to skip.

msgFeedEmpty.message: Nothing to share yet — add a template of your own first. Templates you received from a source are not included.

msgFeedExported.message: Saved $COUNT$ templates to a file. Host it over https, then share the URL.

msgFeedExportedCapped.message: Saved $COUNT$ templates — the most a synced source can hold — so $DROPPED$ were left out. Host the file over https and share the URL.

msgImported.message: Imported — review, then click Save to apply.

msgImportInvalid.message: Import failed: not a valid settings JSON.

msgImportNotOurs.message: Import failed: that file was not exported by this extension.

msgImportIsSyncFile.message: That looks like a template sync file, not a settings backup. Add its URL under Template sync instead.

msgImportNewer.message: Import failed: that backup is from a newer version (schema $FILE$, this build reads $HERE$). Update the extension first.

msgImportUnreadable.message: Import failed: could not read file.

msgSaveFirst.message: Save first — “Sync now” fetches the saved sources.

msgKeptDomains.message: Saved — and kept $SITES$, which was switched on elsewhere while this page was open.
msgKeptDomains.description: Shown instead of "Saved" when the save carried across a domain enabled from the popup or another tab that this page had never displayed. Worth its own message: the alternative was that site quietly going dark, with nothing to connect it to this save.

msgResetConfirm.message:
Reset every setting to its default — including the list of sites this runs on, which empties.
The work items you opened recently or pinned are forgotten too.
Nothing changes until you press Save. When you do, Chrome's access to those sites is handed back as well, so switching one on again means approving it again.
Continue?

msgSavedNoPerm.message: Saved — but site access was denied, so listed domains stay inactive until you grant it.

msgSaveQuota.message: Save failed: settings exceed the ~$LIMIT$ KB Chrome sync allows in total. Shorten or remove templates (or keep a JSON backup).

msgSaveQuotaItem.message: Save failed: your domains and style rules together exceed the ~$LIMIT$ KB Chrome sync allows for one block. Remove some, or keep a JSON backup.

msgSaveTplTooLarge.message: Save failed: the template “$NAME$” is on its own larger than the ~$LIMIT$ KB Chrome sync allows for one block. Shorten it, or keep it in a JSON backup instead.

msgStorageOver.message: — over the sync limit; saving may fail
msgStorageOver.description: Appended to msgStorageUsed. Leading space deliberate.

msgStorageOverItem.message: — one block is over its ~$LIMIT$ KB limit; saving will fail
msgStorageOverItem.description: Appended to msgStorageUsed. Leading space deliberate.

msgStorageNear.description: Appended to msgStorageUsed. Leading space deliberate.

popCopyLabel.description: Heading of the popup's copy block. Doubles as the result line — after a click it is replaced by "Copied." or the missing-field warning, because the popup has no room for a toast.

popNotLoaded.message: Not loaded here — reload the page (Ctrl/Cmd+R).

popNotLoadedShort.message: Not loaded here — reload the page.

popRescanOpen.message: Re-scanned. Open a work item's description.

menuRecent.description: Header over the last templates inserted on this device, shown at the top of a long template menu.

pickHeader.message: Create a rule from a selector  ·  Esc to cancel

pickerHint.message: Click an element to create a rule · Esc to cancel

pickGroupDurable.description: Heading over the first group of picker candidates. The ranking is invisible without it: a reader cannot see an order, and the dimmed rows below read as the normal colour.

pickLifeLasts.description: Per-row verdict on a picker candidate whose handle a person wrote. On every row, not only the bad ones: a mark that shows up only on the exception says nothing on a list with no exception, which is most lists here.

pickLifeChanges.description: Per-row verdict on a picker candidate whose handle the build generated. Pairs with pickLifeLasts — the two chips differ in word and in colour so either one is readable alone.

pickGroupExpiring.message: May not last — generated by the build
pickGroupExpiring.description: Heading over the demoted picker candidates: hashes, uuids, counters. Still pickable — this is a guess about someone else's markup.

pickNoSelector.message: Couldn't build a selector for that element.

pickRuleAdded.message: Rule added: $SELECTOR$ — open Settings to set the value.

pickRuleFailed.message: Failed to save the rule (storage error).

optCopyDesc.message:
The button beside a work item's key, or <kbd>Alt</kbd>/<kbd>⌥</kbd>+<kbd>C</kbd>, copies the item in one of these formats.
The line under each format is exactly what gets copied.

optCopyTokens.message: Three values are filled in: {{item.key}}, {{item.title}} and {{item.url}}. Everything else is copied exactly as typed.

optCopyEmpty.message: No formats yet. Click “Add format” to start.

optCopyFormatPh.description: Placeholder text, and an example of the format language. {{item.key}} and {{item.title}} are tokens the expander looks for — translate around them, never inside them.

focusBtnTitle.message: Turn focus mode on: hide the side panels  ·  Alt+Shift+F (⌥+⇧+F)
focusBtnTitle.description: Title and aria-label of the toggle beside a work item's key. The two states are a matching pair naming the action, not a label and a status line — the pressed state is what says which position it is in. Both name the shortcut, because the button is also where people find out it exists.

focusBtnOnTitle.message: Turn focus mode off: show the side panels  ·  Alt+Shift+F (⌥+⇧+F)

msgCopiedMissing.message: Copied, but $FIELDS$ could not be read — it stayed in the text as written.

msgCopyFailed.message: Could not reach the clipboard. Copy it by hand from the preview in Settings.

msgCopyNoItem.message: No work item on this page — open one, or click a row to open its panel.

msgFocusOn.message: Focus mode on — Alt+Shift+F (⌥+⇧+F) brings the panels back.

msgFocusRestored.message: Focus mode is still on in this tab — Alt+Shift+F (⌥+⇧+F) brings the panels back.
msgFocusRestored.description: Shown once per page load, not on the toggle. A reload is the one way to meet a hidden properties panel without having just asked for it.

msgCopyLimit.message: Up to $MAX$ formats. Remove one to add another.

msgCopyUnknownToken.message: Not a value that can be filled in: $FIELDS$. It is copied as written.

msgExampleAdded.message: Added our example feed. Press Save to fetch it — Chrome will ask for access to raw.githubusercontent.com once.

msgExampleExists.message: Our example feed is already in your sources.

optPermTitle.message: This device needs to approve access

optPermDesc.message: Your settings synced here, but Chrome keeps site access per device — so $COUNT$ of the sites and sources you listed are not approved on this one yet. Until you approve them, the extension stays inactive here.

badgeNeedsAccess.message: Enhancer for Plane — approve access on this device

popPermGap.message: ⚠ Some sites need access on this device — open Settings to approve.

optKeysDesc.message: On macOS, <kbd>Alt</kbd> is the <kbd>⌥</kbd> Option key.

optKeysTplWhere.message: While editing a description, and in the “Create work item” dialog

optKeysCopyWhere.message: On a work item — its own page, or the panel a list opens. Not while you are typing.

optKeysFocus.message: Turn focus mode on or off

optKeysFocusWhere.message: Anywhere the extension runs, including while you are typing

optKeysCtx.message: Open work items from selected text

optKeysRightClick.description: Fills both the Windows and macOS columns of the shortcuts table for the context menu entry — the gesture is the same on both, and leaving a column empty read as unsupported.

optKeysCtxWhere.message: Any page, once you have selected text containing a key

optKeysJump.message: Open a work item by key

optKeysJumpWhere.message: The address bar, on any tab

optKeysThenKey.description: Follows the literal omnibox keyword: “issue” then the key. Not a modifier combination, which is why it reads as words.

optKeysRebind.message: Only the focus mode shortcut can be changed, at chrome://extensions/shortcuts.

optQuickDesc.message: Type issue, a space and a work item key such as PROJ-123 in the address bar, and Enter opens it. The toolbar popup does the same, and so does “Open work items from selection” when you right-click selected text.

optQuickEmpty.message: No quick links yet. Click “Add quick link”.

optQuickPasteLabel.message: Paste an address from your tracker
optQuickPasteLabel.description: Label over the paste box at the top of the quick-link chooser. The examples can only cover trackers we thought of; the reader already has theirs open.

optQuickPastePlaceholder.description: Placeholder in the paste box. An address shaped like the ones it reads, rather than a sentence.

optQuickPasteKnown.message: Read as $NAME$. The search address is filled in too.
optQuickPasteKnown.description: Shown when a pasted address matched one of the known shapes, so nothing is left to type.

optQuickPasteKnownNoSearch.message: Read as $NAME$, which has no address you can search from.
optQuickPasteKnownNoSearch.description: Same as optQuickPasteKnown for a tracker whose example carries no search URL — Linear.

optQuickPasteGuess.message: Not a tracker we know — built from where the key sits in $NAME$'s address. No search address.
optQuickPasteGuess.description: Shown when no known shape matched but a key-shaped path segment was found. Says plainly which part is a guess.

optQuickPasteGuessNumbered.message: Not a tracker we know, and its items are numbered ($NAME$) — choose a prefix to type before the number, like RM-1234.
optQuickPasteGuessNumbered.description: The numbered variant of optQuickPasteGuess. A bare number is not a key, so this one leaves the prefix field to fill.

optQuickPasteUnread.message: No item key found in that address. Open a work item and copy its address, or pick an example below.
optQuickPasteUnread.description: Shown when the pasted text yields nothing. Refusing matters: a template built from a page that is not a work item opens the wrong address forever, silently.

optQuickExamplesLegend.message: ⟨…⟩ is yours to fill in. {{key}} is filled in by the extension.
optQuickExamplesLegend.description: One line at the top of the chooser. The two look alike and mean opposite things, and nothing said so.

optQuickExampleSearchLine.description: The second address on a chooser row. Picking a row fills two fields and the panel was showing one.

optQuickExamplesFromSites.message: From a site you already added
optQuickExamplesFromSites.description: Heading over rows built from the user's own active domains — the host is filled in, so only the workspace is left to type.

optQuickExamplesFromScratch.description: Heading over the per-tracker starting points.

optQuickExamplesBlank.description: The way out of the chooser for someone who wants to type the whole URL themselves.

optQuickExampleNotePlane.message: Search opens the page with your words in the box, but does not run the search.

optQuickExampleNoteLinear.message: No URL you can search from.

optQuickExampleNoteNumbered.message: Issues are numbered, not keyed — type the prefix and the number, e.g. GH-1234.

optQuickUrlPh.description: Placeholder text. {{key}} is a token the expander looks for; the ellipsis stands in for a host. Do not translate either.

optQuickSearchPh.description: Placeholder for the second URL on a quick link row. {{q}} is a token the expander looks for; the ellipsis stands in for a host. Do not translate either.

optQuickApiHint.message: This looks like an API address — opening it shows raw JSON. You probably want the page, e.g. https://…/search/?q={{q}}
optQuickApiHint.description: Hint under a quick link row, not a refusal: an /api/ path can be what someone means. The example is Plane's real search page, verified on app.plane.so.

optQuickSearchPreview.description: Layout only — a phrase, an arrow, the URL it lands on. No words to translate.

optQuickPreview.description: Layout only — a key, an arrow, the URL it lands on. No words to translate.

popRecentClear.description: Popup, at the end of the row of recently opened work items. Forgets them; nothing else.

popRecentClearTitle.message: Forget the work items you opened recently
popRecentClearTitle.description: Tooltip and accessible name for popRecentClear. Plain text: a title, not a pre-line sink.

popPinAdd.description: Toggle on the popup's item line, shown on a work item's tab. The same word in both positions: aria-pressed and the pressed style say which one it is in. It shares a line with the item's title, so keep it short.

popPinAddTitle.message: Pin this item to the popup
popPinAddTitle.description: Tooltip and accessible name for popPinAdd. Plain text: a title, not a pre-line sink.

popPinFull.message: Up to $MAX$ items can be pinned
popPinFull.description: Tooltip and accessible name for the pin button when the list is full and the button is disabled. The button itself shows the count. Plain text.

popPinRemove.description: Tooltip and accessible name for the × on a pinned row. Plain text: a title, not a pre-line sink.

ctxOpenSelection.description: Right-click menu entry, shown only when text is selected. It reads the keys out of whatever was selected and opens each, so the wording says "from selection" rather than naming a key it cannot know yet.

omniboxSearch.description: Omnibox row when what was typed is words rather than a key.

omniboxRecent.description: Omnibox row for a key opened before. The leading word is the only thing that distinguishes these from Chrome's own history rows: the omnibox API offers no per-row icon, so a label is all there is.

omniboxHint.message: Type a work item key to open it, or words to search

omniboxNoTarget.message: No quick link set — Enter opens Settings

optQuickMore.message: The key's prefix picks the link, so ENG- can go to Linear while the rest stays on Plane. The link with an empty prefix takes every other key. In the address, {{key}} is where the key goes, and {{key.proj}} and {{key.num}} are its two halves. The search address is optional: with {{q}} in it, words that are not a key are searched there. A selection can hold several keys, and each opens in its own tab, up to 10 at once.
optQuickMore.description: Settings › Quick open, inside More. One sentence per line.

optTplMore.message: The body is Markdown: ## headings, - and 1. lists, - [ ] checkboxes, **bold** and `code`. Filled in on insert: {{date}}, {{date+7}} or any other number of days, {{week}} for Monday to Sunday, {{month}}, and your own {{var.name}}. Share with your team saves your own templates as a file. Put it anywhere your teammates can reach over https, and they add that address under Template sync.

optFocusMore.message: Hiding the properties panel and hiding the left navigation are on from the start, and a reading-width rule ships switched off. Focus mode lasts for the tab you turned it on in, survives a reload, and ends when you close the tab. It never syncs to your other devices. To rebind the shortcut, open chrome://extensions/shortcuts.

optKeysWhyTitle.message: Why can't the others be changed?
optKeysWhyTitle.description: Summary of a disclosure on the Shortcuts tab.

optKeysWhy.message: Alt+T and Alt+C are handled inside the page, where Chrome offers no way to rebind them. Alt+C does nothing while you type, because on macOS ⌥+C is the character “ç”. Chrome has no way to rename the issue keyword either. For a shorter one, add your own under Site search at chrome://settings/searchEngines, pointing at https://your-plane/your-workspace/browse/%s. That opens one fixed address: no prefixes, no recent items and no search.
optKeysWhy.description: Inside the disclosure on the Shortcuts tab. One sentence per line.

optMore.description: Summary of the collapsed details under a settings card's description.

optFieldOpen.description: Short label beside a quick link's address field.

optFieldSearch.description: Short label beside a quick link's search address field.

optFieldTitle.description: Short label beside a template's title field.

optFieldBody.description: Short label beside a template's body field.

optFieldName.description: Short label beside a template's name field.

optSyncEnabled.description: Beside the Template sync card's own switch. Not optEnabled: that one names the whole extension in Korean.
